messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Submit Button
parts:
Right now the submitButton function adds a submit button to the page, which halts execution of every reactive component on the page. Is it possible for the submit button to be attached only to a specific output component so that reactivity is maintained on the rest of the page?

If there is an alternate way to achieve this, that would be appreciated as well.

Thanks.

I have used actionButton in several parts of my app and having to use devtools, Rtools, etc. makes distribution more complicated than it might have to be. It also makes Shiny less 'available' to new developers that do not want to compile from source packages.


On Thursday, February 7, 2013 11:14:50 AM UTC-8, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
This approach should work:
https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!topic/shiny-discuss/l8ZcauoOtuw

Note that you'll need to install shiny-incubator to use actionButton:
install.package("devtools")  # if necessary
devtools::install_github("shiny-incubator", "rstudio")

If there is an alternate way to achieve this, that would be appreciated as well.

Thanks.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Submit Button
parts:
I was thinking you could add an R function "select2Input", that is *very* roughly:

select2Input <- function(inputId, ...) {
  tagList(
    tags$script(src="select2.js"),
    selectInput(inputId=inputId, ...),
    tags$script(paste("$(function() { $('#", inputId, "').select2(); });", sep=""))
  )
}

On Fri, Feb 8, 2013 at 6:10 AM, David P <davidp...@gmail.com> wrote:
Joe,

Not to steal Vincent's thunder or anything, but over the weekend, I posted to the following thread expressing interest to see how you would convert something like "select2" to a fully functioning widget within Shiny:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/T4NL74DtDdI

Like Vincent, I have tried to convert it using some of the techniques discussed in other threads on this board, but have run into a roadblock when getting it to function under the reactiveUI context. I am pretty sure it requires following the process laid out in the "building-inputs" Shiny webpage. However, I am unsure which of the select2 functions to encapsulate in the methods laid out in "building-inputs". If you could demonstrate how to perform such a conversion, it could be extremely useful going forward for others to model the same conversion procedure for additional javascript tools.

Thanks again for all the work you continue to do with the Shiny package,
David 

Here is another link to Vincent's code:
https://github.com/mostly-harmless/select2shiny
Thanks for providing this template, Vincent!

Keep in mind that the CRAN folks like to keep updates to less than once every 1-2 months, so you might want to get the additional functions in there before submitting to CRAN.

Vincent, I'm sorry but can you remind me exactly what you needed from me? If we talked about this in a thread I seem to have lost it, sorry.
